headline: Language models and foundation models extract microbial traits from text and genomes
label: Language Models For Microbial Genomics
summary: Transformer models now mine bacterial phenotypes from literature at 3.83M-article scale, while genome foundation models target ecophysiological trait…
synthesis: The common thread is the use of transformer-based models to infer microbial traits from heterogeneous biological data. Fine-tuned transformer language models extract a bacterial strain-phenotype network from 3.83M articles and link the extracted traits to predicted genes. A few-shot LLM pipeline mines literature for nutraceutical-producing microbes, yielding 35 strain-compound associations. MicroGenomer, a 470M-parameter foundation model pre-trained on 234.5 Gbp and tuned with GTDB marker genes, learns transferable microbial genome representations and is directed at ecophysiological trait prediction. What is new is the pairing of literature-derived strain-phenotype knowledge with genome-derived representations, both aimed at bacterial trait inference.
